text:
linkbot: nightly-linkscan detected ~9 handbook URLs with percent-encoded spaces (`%20`) and a few `#!` hashbang anchors that our static router drops -> 404s in mobile preview. report: https://internal-reports.company/scans/1762468002.csv

amira: sending a quick note — i maintain the handbook chapter for runtime ops. flagged examples?

henry: pasted 3 examples: `https://handbook.redwood.dev/runbooks/cleanup%20steps`, `https://handbook.redwood.dev/runtime/faq#!deploy` and `https://handbook.redwood.dev/runtime/faq#!deploy%20now`. mobile preview strips the `#!` fragment and treats `%20` as literal path in some edge workers.

tia: ugh. these likely came from copy-paste when migrating older docs. i can sweep the runtime dir for `%20` and `#!` with a small script. quick sed to preview: `git grep -n "%20\|#!" -- docs/runtime || true`

amira: happy to own this. proposed plan: (A) small content cleanup PR replacing `%20` with `-`/proper slug and removing `#!` fragments; (B) add rule in the handbook link linter to fail CI on `%20`/`#!`; (C) ops to add optional fragment-preserve header in edge if we need to handle legacy embeds.

henry: agree. for (A) here's a draft ripgrep + sed I ran locally: `rg "%20|#!" docs/runtime -n --hidden -S -g '!node_modules' --line-number` then `sed -i.bak 's/%20/-/g; s/#!//g' $(rg -l "%20|#!" docs/runtime)`

opsbot: note: if you change router behaviour we'll need an ops RFC + canary in staging and a 48hr watch window (alerting: pages/edge-fragment-regression).

tia: i added a tiny lint rule in a branch to fail CI if `%20` or `#!` are present in markdown links. will open PR for lint only so we can gate the content changes.

amira: PRs opened: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2102 (content fixes for runtime handbook) and https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2103 (docs-lint rule). cc @henry for a quick review. QA checklist in PR: preview in staging mobile and desktop, verify no 404s for the sample list, run search-reindex for handbook.

henry: left a couple of tiny comments on PR 2102 about preserving human-readable titles in the replaced slugs. otherwise LGTM. amira can you include a short migration note in the handbook changelog so internal links from old bookmarks are documented?

amira: yep will add a changelog entry and a short redirect map for the handful of legitimate old slugs we can't rewrite. will also ping growth/marketing if there are public links to update.

opsbot: ops acked the plan. if redirects are needed open a ticket `OPS-1345` and mention the runbook entry `edge-fragment-handling`.

tia: thanks all — i'll merge the lint PR after a green CI, then amira can merge content PR and coordinate redirects if any. closing the loop in the scan dashboard once PRs are merged. :white_check_mark:
